summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including type 1 diabetes, failed renal and pancreas transplants, end-stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis, and autonomic neuropathy was admitted due to elevated INR over 9 and pink dialysate, concerning for bleeding. She also presented with hypoglycemia-related altered mental status, pleuritic chest pain, and poor oral intake. Vitamin K was given for the coagulopathy, warfarin was held and later restarted at 1 mg daily as the INR normalized. The pink dialysate resolved. A CT chest showed bilateral pleural effusions and a right apical opacity, but no signs of active infection; antibiotics were not needed. Tacrolimus was reduced due to a high level. Malnutrition was addressed with nutritional support. She remained stable, was discharged to extended care, and will follow up with her transplant, nephrology, and cardiology teams.
problems: Peripheral autonomic neuropathy in disorders classified elsewhere
Diabetes with other specified manifestations, type I [juvenile type], not stated as uncontrolled

Diabetes with ophthalmic manifestations, type I [juvenile type], not stated as uncontrolled
